conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that the claim is supported, citing trial and meta-analysis evidence demonstrating that tenofovir disoproxil fumarate started in late pregnancy reduces mother-to-child transmission of hepatitis B in women with high viral loads.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion:** The claim is supported: for pregnant people with chronic HBV and *high maternal HBV DNA*, tenofovir disoproxil fumarate (TDF) started late in pregnancy lowers the residual risk of mother-to-child transmission when added to standard newborn prevention (hepatitis-B vaccine, and hepatitis-B immune globulin where used).

**Key evidence**

- A pivotal randomized trial in highly viremic mothers found transmission of **5% with TDF versus 18% without maternal antiviral treatment**—an absolute reduction of 13 percentage points. TDF was used in late pregnancy and infants also received immunoprophylaxis. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/nejmoa1508660  
- A second placebo-controlled trial starting at 28 weeks found **0/147** infant infections with TDF versus **3/147** with placebo. The difference was not statistically definitive, largely because rigorous infant immunoprophylaxis made transmission uncommon in both groups; it therefore does not negate the overall benefit, but shows the incremental effect can be hard to measure where newborn prevention is very effective. https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1708131  
- A systematic review/meta-analysis concluded that peripartum antiviral prophylaxis is highly effective and supports WHO’s recommendation for pregnancy use of TDF to prevent HBV transmission. https://www.thelancet.com/journals/laninf/article/PIIS1473-3099(20)30586-7/fulltext  

**Important qualification:** This is targeted prophylaxis—not evidence that every HBsAg-positive pregnant person needs tenofovir. Maternal viral load is central because higher HBV DNA predicts transmission risk. Infant birth-dose vaccination (and HBIG when available/indicated) remains essential; TDF supplements rather than replaces it.
